Hypothesis: Students with more consistent first-four-week engagement will have a lower probability of being at risk.
EDA evidence: Successful students had median 231 clicks and 12 active days, compared with 119 clicks and 7 active days for at-risk students.

Hypothesis: Students with no VLE activity during days 0-27 will have a higher probability of later failure or withdrawal.
EDA evidence: The at-risk rate was 81.4% with no activity, compared with 42.4% with some activity.

Hypothesis: Students who do not submit an available early assessment will have a higher probability of being at risk.
EDA evidence: The at-risk rate was 85.1% for non-submitters and 39.6% for submitters.

Hypothesis: Higher early assessment scores will be associated with a lower probability of being at risk.
EDA evidence: After excluding the unusual near-binary assessment 15020, risk declined from 90.6% below score 40 to 26.2% at score 80 or above.

Hypothesis: Students with more previous attempts will have a higher probability of being at risk.
EDA evidence: Risk increased from 41.8% with no previous attempts to 66.2% with two or more attempts.

Hypothesis: Students studying more credits will have a higher probability of being at risk.
EDA evidence: Risk increased from 41.8% for up to 60 credits to 61.1% for more than 180 credits.

Hypothesis: At-risk rates and predictive relationships will differ between modules and presentations.
EDA evidence: Module risk ranged from 26.0% for AAA to 52.4% for CCC, with further variation between presentations.

Hypothesis: Model performance may differ across demographic and socioeconomic groups and should be evaluated separately.
EDA evidence: Risk varied by disability, age, education, gender, and area-deprivation band. These are associations, not causal conclusions.
